articleTitle: An Approach to Finite-Time $\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$ Control of T-S Fuzzy Systems via Piecewise Lyapunov Functions
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of finite-time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$</tex> control of Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy models. By using the piecewise Lyapunov function and the finite-time Lyapunov theorem, a new controller design scheme is proposed such that the closed-loop fuzzy control system is finite-time stable with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$</tex> performance. It is shown that the proposed controller and its corresponding piecewise Lyapunov function, which is continuous across subspace boundaries, can be designed by solving a set of bilinear matrix inequalities (BMIs). Moreover, an upper bound on the time required for finite-time convergence of the fuzzy control system can be estimated. Finally, numerical simulations are used to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: Traffic Flow Prediction Based on Spatial-Temporal Sparse Attention Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Since traffic data has dynamic spatial and temporal dependence features. So timely and accurate traffic forecasting, especially in the medium and long term, remains a challenging problem. For medium and long time prediction, this paper proposes a multi-time granularity spatial-temporal sparse attention model (MGSTSA). The model utilizes the periodic characteristics of traffic data and introduces new spatial-temporal blocks to learn the dynamic spatial and temporal dependence of traffic data at different time granularities. Specifically, the spatial block models local spatial relationships and global spatial relationships for long-distance road segments with similar traffic patterns via GCN and multi-headed sparse self-attention. The temporal block models long-time dependencies using temporal sparse attention networks. Dynamic spatial-temporal dependencies under different features are extracted by combining multiple temporal granularities. The proposed method is evaluated on Xi'an and Jinan traffic speed datasets. Comparing with the better performing GWNET in the baselines, the proposed model reduces the mean absolute error by 16.1 % and 11.3% on the two datasets, for 2 hours forecasting.

articleTitle: Path Following Control of Unmanned Surface Vehicle Based on Improved Line-of-Sight Method
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of inaccurate path following control of unmanned surface vehicle under the conventional line-of-sight method, a path-following controller for unmanned surface vehicle based on the improved line-of-sight method was designed. Firstly, the conventional line-of-sight method guidance process was analyzed, and the path following control problem was transformed into the heading angle deviation control and the target waypoint update problem. Then, the adaptive sight circle radius value was used to replace the original fixed sight circle radius value to realize dynamic adjustment of the sight circle. The back-stepping method was used to improve the path following control method to precisely control the longitudinal speed of the unmanned surface vehicle. Finally, the effectiveness of the improved method was verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Finite-Time Prescribed Performance Synchronization for Complex Dynamical Networks Based on Event-Triggered Pinning Control
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper studies the finite-time prescribed performance synchronization of complex dynamical network under event-triggered mechanism and pinning control. A new finite-time prescribed performance function and event-triggered pinning controller are designed. Some sufficient conditions are proposed to ensure the synchronization can be realized. An easy-to-implement selection algorithm is adopted to update the pinning node set. A theoretical analysis is proved that the strategy can avoid the occurrence of Zeno phenomenon. Lastly, the effectiveness of the results is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Robot Path Planning Adopting Improved Artificial Potential Field Method by Normal Random Particles
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The robot path planning often fails when the traditional APF(Artificial Potential Field) method is applied. Because the local minimum problem often appears in APF method. Normal distribution random particles are introduced to solve the problem above. A series of random particles are generated around the local minimum path planning point. The cost function is newly defined to select the particle which is far from the obstacle and close to the target point. The selected particle is applied as the path planning point instead of the local minimum point. The validity of the improved APF algorithm is verified by simulation using the matplotlib module in Python scripts. The simulation results show that the algorithm is feasible.

articleTitle: A Visual Bionic Neural Encoder Based on NPC Memristor for Spiking Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: As a new generation of neural networks, neuron-based spiking neural network (SNN) neuromorphic computing has become the focus of research, which utilizes biological plausible neurons to provide faster inference and lower energy consumption. In the hardware implementation of the spiking neural network, a hardware encoder part similar to the sensory neuron is needed to convert external stimuli into pulsed signals (spike train) according to the neural algorithm and the corre-sponding learning rules. Unfortunately, most traditional Spiking neural network circuits use digital circuit technology as the input, but most of the information in the real world is in the form of analog information, so neural encoders need to be developed to meet the growing demand for neuromorphic computation. This paper presents a hardware encoding design for neurons based on a negative photoconductive memristor that converts optical signals into count-based pulsed neural encoding. Finally, the proposed bionic encoding device is used to encode the MNIST dataset, and then the trained SNN is used to make an accuracy judgment of over 97.38%. Based on this, a bionic hierarchical visual perception system is designed.

articleTitle: Research on Algorithm for Guidance Information Extraction of Rotational Bias Passive Radar Seeker
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Research on the guidance information extraction algorithm for a rotating biased passive radar seeker applied to aircraft. The angle measurement information of the rotary bias seeker not only couples the attitude angle of the missile body, but also its installation bias angle and rotation angle relative to the missile body. To isolate the installation bias angle and rotation angle in the angle measurement information, a rotation solving algorithm is designed to obtain the estimated misalignment angle of the non spin and non bias strapdown seeker. A misalignment angle interpolation algorithm is designed to address the intermittent detection problem caused by the oblique rotation of the seeker, and the misalignment angle estimation value at the blind spot of the field of view is obtained. Isolate the attitude angle of the estimated misalignment angle after spinning and interpolation, and design a guidance information reconstruction algorithm based on alpha-beta filtering to obtain the estimated line of sight angle and line of sight angle rate of the equivalent active seeker. Experimental analysis shows that the designed rotation solving algorithm and misalignment angle interpolation algorithm can be applied to the design of guidance information extraction algorithms under the rotating bias seeker system.

articleTitle: Smoke and Fire Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Human life and property, as well as the environment, are seriously threatened by fire. Whether fire can be quickly and effectively detected and timely warned is of great significance to maintain daily life and social security. To address the shortcomings of previous algorithms, a smoke and fire detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv5 is proposed. Firstly, adding SimAM attention module in network to improve the feature extraction ability of the algorithm without additional parameters; Then replacing the coupled head with an improved decoupled head in Head layer to improve the network performance; Finally, the loss function is redesigned by replacing the original CloU loss with Focal EloU loss, which can effectively deal with the sample class imbalance problem and improve the detection accuracy in complex background. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the improved algorithm is improved to 91.6%, improves the detection accuracy of small targets in complex backgrounds, and reduces the problem of false alarms and missed alarms.

articleTitle: A Flame Localization Method Combing Visible-Light and Near-Infrared Cameras
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: As common natural disasters, fire incidents seriously threaten human life and property. Flame target localization is a key step to enabling timely detection and effective control of the fire incident. In this study, a novel approach that combines visible-light and near-infrared cameras in a heterogeneous binocular camera system is proposed. High-precision localization of early small-scale fire targets is achieved through calibration of the heterogeneous binocular camera, stereo rectification, heterogeneous disparity matching, and depth computation. Experimental tests were conducted within a range of 1–5 meters, validating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Low-Voltage Apparatus Assembly Quality Inspection Network Based on ConvNeXt
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Assembly quality inspection, which aims to detect misplaced, missing, and broken defects in products and classify defective products from normal ones, plays a significant role in ensuring the final quality of low-voltage apparatus. The huge production quantity makes manual inspection time-consuming and laborious, and consistency difficult to guarantee. This paper proposes a ConvNeXt-based classification network that introduces the 3D non-parametric attention module SimAM Block and adapts output accordingly. It fully integrates features of different scales and levels to obtain rich contour texture and semantic information of low-voltage apparatuses. The experimental results show this method has an accuracy of 97.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on the test dataset of low-voltage apparatus images. Ablation experiments verify the improved module framework.

articleTitle: Intelligent Ship Navigation Method Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of autonomous ship collision avoidance, this study proposes an autonomous ship obstacle avoidance method that combines the D-star algorithm and the twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) algorithm. In this study, the obstacle zone by target (OZT) and virtual grid sensors are introduced as inputs to the observation state; the environment state is directly mapped to the ship's steering commands as the output of the algorithm. In terms of the reward function design, by combining the collision avoidance reward function with the quantitatively classified navigational situation, it ensures that the ship's collision avoidance decision-making behavior complies with COLREGs (International Regulations for Preventing Collision at Sea). The simulation experiment results show that the proposed method can effectively simplify the input problem of the model and successfully output the current observation state space. At the same time, the method is flexible and scalable, and is able to solve the multi-ship autonomous collision avoidance problem in compliance with the COLREGs rules.

articleTitle: Insulator and Spacer Dataset and Benchmark for Power Inspection
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In the field of power inspection based on object detection, high-quality, multi-scenario inspection dataset is of great significance for accurate detection of power equipment. But due to various conditions, the currently open source power inspection dataset contains less image information, which limits the effect of the algorithm in actual operation. In order to achieve better object detection effect in power inspection, this paper establishes an insulator and spacer dataset, which improves the reliability and robustness of the algorithm in power inspection by introducing more image features and more complex background information. Experimental results show that the new dataset combined with YOLOV5 series algorithms can maintain high image recognition accuracy in the process of complex environment detection. In addition, we have made lightweight improvements to Yolov5, which reduces GFLOPs by 27%, detection time by 24% compared to YOLOV5n, achieving better balance in insulator and spacer dataset with 89.1 % accuracy on mAP50, and is more suitable for deployment in edge platforms.

articleTitle: Research on Space-Ground Collaborative Fault Diagnosis Technology in Satellite Based on LSTM
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The continuous increase in the number of satellites in orbit places a great burden on the management of ground operations and makes it difficult to deal with failures that occur in orbit in a timely and effective manner. With the rapid development of intelligent technology and the improvement of on-board computing capability, a kind of Space-ground Collaborative satellite fault diagnosis environment was established, which formed a base of ground intelligent algorithms including long short-term memory network algorithms, and deployed the trained models at the on-board to verify the fault diagnosis of the key equipment TT &C fixed relays that affect satellite safety. The results showed that the method could effectively diagnose the faults of the satellite's key components, It can increase the intelligence levels of satellite.

articleTitle: An Imitation Learning and Reinforcement Learning Approach to Power System Stabilizer
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of power system structures, ensuring stability in power systems has become a significant challenge. This paper proposes a combined approach of imitation learning and reinforcement learning for designing power system stabilizers. The method involves collecting input-output data from conventional power system stabilizers as expert demonstrations and utilizing supervised learning to pretrain the policy, thereby initializing the reinforcement learning agent. The agent then interacts with the power system simulation environment to learn the optimal action policy and enhance power system stability. Simulation results on a four-machine two-area power system demonstrate that this technique outperforms traditional power system stabilizers in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Resilient Consensus Control of Nonlinear Second-Order MASs Under DoS Attacks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper focuses on the coordinated control of multi-agent systems (MASs) and proposes an event-triggered control strategy to conserve computing resource and alleviate the impact of Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. MASs have become an important research topic due to its potential applications in various fields and the abilities of multiple agents to interact and cooperate enables them to perform complex tasks. However, DoS attacks can prevent agents from obtaining useful information and disrupt communication channels, leading to instability of the MASs. The proposed strategy allows agents to update their states only when certain triggering conditions are met, thus reducing communication frequency and improving efficiency and robustness. This paper proposes resilient controller for achieving practical consensus in second-order directed MASs under DoS attacks, demonstrating the feasibility of the scheme through Lyapunov functions and comparison principles. Simulation results show that the proposed method is effective in mitigating the impact of DoS attacks and achieving consensus.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of the New Energy Hybrid Ship System via Improved Grey Wolf Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the rapid growth of energy consumption, the application of traditional ship brings more and more serious problems of energy consumption and pollution to the marine environment. To solve this problem, an optimal energy scheduling strategy for new energy hybrid ship system based on improved gray wolf algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the new energy hybrid ship system model consisted of diesel generator, photovoltaic power system and energy storage system is established. Con-sidering the operating cost and carbon emissions, an optimal objective function is established. Meanwhile, an improved gray wolf optimization algorithm is introduced to handle the above energy scheduling problem. Finally, simulation result is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the improved grey wolf algorithm-based optimal energy scheduling strategy for the new energy hybrid ship system.

articleTitle: An Improved Real-Time Detection Method for Flame and Smoke Identification Based on YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Fire is a very harmful disaster, which seriously threatens people's life and property safety, so the detection and early warning of fire is very important. With the development of deep learning, smoke, and fire detection technology has become very mature. Despite this, the flame recognition algorithm based on YOLOv5s still has the disadvantages of slow calculation speed, low accuracy, and high false detection and missing rate. To solve this problem, this paper proposes an improved flame and smoke detection algorithm based on the YOLOv5s network, mainly studying how to improve the efficiency and accuracy of flame and smoke detection. First, the fully Attentional network (FLAnet) is introduced to enhance the simultaneous encoding space and channel attention of a single similar graph, and improve the global computing efficiency; Secondly, CoordConv is introduced to make it have space awareness, can carry out identity mapping, and improve the learning rate, and named FC-YOLO. Finally, according to the data set, data enhancement technology and label smoothing are used to preprocess the sample set, which solves the overfitting problem caused by insufficient sample number. The experimental results show that the average mAP@0.5 value is 73.6%, 3.5% higher than the original model. The improved network model has higher detection accuracy, improves the efficiency of fire monitoring, helps to reduce the loss caused by fire, and has great practical significance.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Switched Gain Adaptive LMI Sliding Mode Control for VSP Propulsion Ship Dynamic Positioning
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This article focuses on ships equipped with Voith Schneider Propellers (VSP) and establishes a mathematical model for the 3-DOF motion of VSP propulsion ship in dynamic positioning (DP); To address environmental disturbances encountered during dynamic positioning, a sliding mode disturbance observer (SMDO) is designed to estimate and compensate for unknown bounded disturbances; Additionally, in order to improve the accuracy of ship dynamic positioning control, a linear matrix inequality (LMI) sliding mode robust controller is designed in conjunction with the disturbance observer, which transforms the control problem into an optimization problem with linear inequality constraints; To mitigate chattering during sliding mode control, a bidirectional switching gain adaptive item is introduced to strengthen the negative regulation ability of the gain. Simulation results show that the designed controller can maintain system stability in the presence of external disturbances, with fast convergence speed.

articleTitle: A Solution to the Problem of Self-Interference Under Multi-Robot Cooperative Exploration with 2D Lidar
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Multi-robot cooperative exploration is more efficient in constructing unknown environment maps, compared with single-robot autonomous exploration. However, it is inevitable to identify each other as obstacles in exploration, resulting in self-interference. We propose an anti-self-interference problem framework, aiming at the self-interference problem in multi-robot collaborative exploration. First, the initial position of the dynamic obstacle is judged by the coordinate relationship between the robots; second, considering that there is a certain error in the coordinate system conversion relationship, the DBSCAN algorithm is used to cluster the lidar data, and the ICP algorithm is used to realize the dynamic obstacle object tracking. The anti-self-interference framework proposed in this paper improves the success rate of exploration tasks and the quality of the map by continuously eliminating the lidar point cloud data generated by dynamic obstacles. At the same time, the robot relies on the original lidar data to perform real-time dynamic path planning tasks and achieves accurate construction of static maps under the premise of ensuring the safety of multiple robots. Finally, a large number of simulation results in the gazebo simulation scene confirm that the proposed method is effective.

articleTitle: Co-Design of Underwater Detection and Communication-Part I: Detection-Based Shared Waveform
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Existing underwater detection and communication systems are usually isolated. Detection and communication work separately, but they have some functional similarities. If the two are not focused on another one receiving data, then it will make the detection and communication systems in the spectrum source and energy consumption compete with each other, which decreases the performance of the entire system. Therefore, the construction of an integrated underwater detection and commu-nication architecture is necessary. This article proposes a design method for a shared waveform based on the detection signal and analyzes its performance. The idea is that the detection signal, the generalized sinusoidal frequency modulation (GSFM), is modulated by the minimum Gaussian shift keying (GMSK) to obtain the ultimate integrated waveform with detection and communication capabilities. Firstly, the article introduces the orthogonality of the GSFM detection signal and the G MSK modulation and demodulation processes, after which the two integrate into a shared signal. Then compare the ambiguity function of the shared waveform and the GSFM waveform, analyzing the detection performance of the shard waveform. Compare the bit error rate (BER) of the shared waveform with the GMSK signal, analyzing the communication performance of the shared waveform. The simulation results show that the shared waveform possesses the capabilities of detection and communication. Its performance is conformed to the characteristics of shared waveform based on detection signal design in fully shared systems.

articleTitle: Target-fencing control of multi-agent systems with input saturation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, we studied the problem of stationary target-fencing control for multi-agent systems with input saturation constraints. The distributed controller is designed by using low gain feedback and saturation functions that use distances between neighboring agents and distances between each agent and the target. The law does not need to pre-specify the shape of the agents' formation to achieve target-fencing, and collision avoid-ance between agents is guaranteed. The stability of the controller is demonstrated by the Lyapunov method. Finally, the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed control law.

articleTitle: Research on the Hardness Identification Method of Rock Wall for Shearer Based on SSA-VMD-SSAE
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The hardness of underground rock walls in coal mines varies significantly, and the cutting teeth of the shearer are prone to damage during the cutting process. However, it is challenging to identify the hardness of rock walls in the complex underground environment. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hardness identification method for shearer's rock wall cutting based on the improved Sparse Spike Assignment Variational Mode Decomposition (SSA-VMD) combined with Stacked Sparse Autoencoders (SSAE). The proposed method utilizes the collected cantilever vibration signals and employs the SSA-VMD algorithm with an improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (SSA) to determine the penalty factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> and the decomposition layers K. Then, it combines the wavelet packet energy features and time-domain features of each mode component to construct a hybrid feature vector. Finally, the hybrid feature vector is inputted into a recognition model composed of stacked sparse autoencoders and a softmax layer to output the hardness identification results. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving a recognition accuracy of 98.6%, which is significantly higher than other commonly used identification methods.

articleTitle: An improved grey wolf optimization algorithm for parameter tuning of active disturbance rejection control
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The performance of active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) is determined by its suitable parameters. It is difficult to obtain a satisfactory solution using conventional empirical tuning methods. An improved grey wolf optimization algorithm (IGWO) is proposed to tune the ADRC's parameters in this work. In particular, the chaotic mapping and nonlinear convergence factor improvement strategies are presented to overcome the tendency of GWO to fall into the local optimum problem when initializing populations. A second-order system is selected to verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme. The results demonstrated that the proposed method can be used for parameter tuning of ADRC.

articleTitle: Object Detection for Intelligent Driving Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Developing intelligent driving has great potential to enhance traffic safety and reduce economic losses. However, the existing object detection algorithms suffer from large model parameters and high computational complexity, making them difficult to deploy on resource-constrained devices. Lightweight algorithms often sacrifice model accuracy. In this paper, we propose a lightweight YOLOv5 structure (YOLOv5-ODE), which greatly improves the computational efficiency without losing the feature expression ability, by introducing the GGhostRegNet module with low computational burden and the ECA attention mechanism. We innovatively propose a lightweight attention-downs amp ling module, named DeformCAConv, which can be integrated into different stages of the model for better learning of global features and local irregular features. The experi-mental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed lightweight network. Specifically, compared with YOLOv5s, under 54.4% FLOPs reduction, YOLOv5-ODE improves by 1.3% on mAP@0.5:0.95.

articleTitle: Distributed Fixed-Time Control of Inverter Air Conditioners Based on Consensus Strategy
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the depletion of global resources, the regulation and control of power system has attached more and more importance. Besides, the demand for operating reserve to maintain the power system balance is increasing. With traditional generating units phasing out, it is concerned that they may become inadequate to meet the reserve requirement in the near future. Thus, the demand-side management is becoming increasingly important. Inverter air conditioners (IACs) account for a larger proportion in the power consumption. Nevertheless, the control and optimization of distributed IACs is complicated. To address the above-mentioned issues, this manuscript proposes a distributed control strategy for the regulation of IACs. Based on the consensus theory, the states convergence and the power regulation of IACs is realized within the settling time. By utilizing Lyapunov stability theorem and consensus theory, the convergence of control strategy is verified. Finally, the simulation results are given to demonstrate the effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on Path Planning Control of Maze Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: To solve the problem of slow exploration speed of maze robot, a new kind of maze robot is designed in this paper. STM32FI03C8T6 with strong performance is used as the control chip to effectively improve the working efficiency of maze robot. The existing left-right exploration algorithms are compared and optimized, and the left-right cross algorithm is proposed, which effectively improves the maze exploration speed and accuracy of the maze robot. The experimental platform of the maze robot is built, and the path exploration and control program of the robot is verified. The results show that the designed maze robot can effectively explore the path, the hardware system can reduce the influence of external environmental factors such as light and temperature on the maze robot, and improve the motion control stability and exploration algorithm accuracy of the maze robot.

articleTitle: BERT and Word Segmentation Algorithm Research on the Relationship Between Diabetes Symptoms and Traditional Chinese Medicine
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Diabetes is a common chronic Metabolic disorder, and its treatment has always been a hot research topic in the medical field. Traditional Chinese medicine has a significant therapeutic effect on it and has become one of the important ways for patients to choose treatment methods. In recent years, with the development and application of deep learning technology, more and more research has begun to attempt to use deep learning models to process traditional Chinese medicine case data, achieving automated information extraction and analysis. This study shows that BERT model and jieba segmentation algorithm have good effect in the study of the relationship between symptoms and Medication in diabetes medical record data, which is expected to provide scientific basis and reference for clinical treatment of traditional Chinese medicine.

articleTitle: Path Planning of Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Departing from Port Based on Improved Deep Q-Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper presents a path planning scheme for autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) in port environment based on improved Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm. First, port map is gridded and binarized, and port area is separated from other areas according to port shape. Secondly, in order to enable the agent to leave port area, the range of agent exploration randomness is increased in port area. Finally, to solve the problem that the traditional DQN algorithm is difficult to make the agent find the target point after leaving port area quickly, the reward function of DQN is improved. Simulation results verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Research on the Integrated Guidance and Control with Sigular Perturbation Theory
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the increasing requirements of unmanned aerial vehicle (UA V) for information extraction and situational awareness, the design of integrated guidance and control system should serve the needs of sensors. Therefore, in order to improve the detection accuracy better, this paper focus on the problem of guidance information extraction and guidance control of the UA V using the offset rotating strap down seeker. Considering the influence of the offset rotating strapdown seeker on the dynamics characteristics of the UA V and the guidance accuracy constraints, the reduced order decoupling of the guidance and control integration model is realized on the base of the singular perturbation method, and the subsystem controllers are designed by the sliding mode control theory. The feasibility of the proposed controller is verified by mathematical simulation.

articleTitle: A New Distributed Sliding Mode Controller Design for Multi-Agent Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper focuses on analyzing the issue of achieving asymptotic consensus in second-order multi-agent systems. The research introduces a novel dynamic sliding mode control technique that ensures the sliding surface is reached within a finite time. Through simulation experiments, the viability of the suggested approach is validated.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Demand Response of Thermal Storage Electric Boilers
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper proposes a comprehensive optimization method for participating in demand response in a centralized heating system mainly composed of thermal storage electric boilers. A physical model of the heat supply process at the heat source station is established, and an optimization algorithm is designed based on the participation process. The algorithm starts from the perspective of the load aggregators with the objective of minimizing overall costs to improve users' willingness to participate in demand response. Simulations based on examples are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the method, and the differences in operating strategies before and after optimization are analyzed.

articleTitle: High-Precision Indoor Positioning for Drone Based on EfficientNetV2 and CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the development of smart hardware devices and the increasing demand for indoor positioning, Wi-Fi Re-ceived Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI)-based fingerprinting has become a simple and low-hardware requirement method for indoor positioning. However, in complex indoor environments, signal attenuation and multipath effects can severely interfere with wireless signal propagation, thereby reducing positioning accuracy. This paper proposes a new positioning scheme that uses an EfficientNetV2 classification model and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) regression model. The scheme first converts RSSI values into feature maps, then uses the EfficientNetV2 model to classify the wall where the drone is located, narrowing down the positioning area. Then the feature maps are input into the proposed CNN model to estimate three-dimensional coordinates and improve positioning accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves an average error of 2.01 meters in three-dimensional positioning Euclidean distance, compared to 2.14 meters for the traditional method, resulting in a 6.07 % improvement in positioning accuracy. These results demonstrate the advantages of the new method in overcoming signal interference in indoor environments and effectively improving positioning accuracy.

articleTitle: Anti-Wind and Wave Interference Control of Sea Gangway Based on DDPG Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Aiming at the control problem of ship-borne sea gangway under the in interference of wind and waves, the kinematic model of gangway is built by D-H parameter method, and the kinematic equation of the gangway is deduced. Then, the reward function sets the target point guidance, self-collision detection and training round limit as rewards and punishments, introduces the deep reinforcement learning DDPG algorithm to learn the action-reward model, and uses the learning results to manipulate the movement of the gangway in pursuit of higher reward value. Finally, a model is built in the simulation platform gazebo, and wind and wave interference is introduced into the Marine System Simulator (MSS) toolbox to train the model. The results show that after a certain number of training episodes, the end of the gangway can be stabilized in the specified position. Experimental results show that the convergence speed and efficiency of this method are good.

articleTitle: Distributed Predefined-Time Economic Dispatching for Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Along with the promotion and application of new energy, the widespread access of distributed power makes the structure of microgrid complex and changeable. The centralized optimization method is no longer available for solving the problem of economic dispatching due to its operation mode and nature. In this paper, a distributed optimization method is designed to solve the economic dispatching problem of microgrid by applying the predefined-time consensus-based algorithm in multi-agent system, where the micro increment of generator set cost is taken as consensus variable. This algorithm can directly set an upper bound of optimal time, so that the power output of all generators in the grid can be controlled cooperatively within a specified time. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by simulation and analysis.

articleTitle: Q-Learning Control for Robust $H_{\infty}$ Tracking of De-Oiling Hydrocyclone Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: A de-oiling hybrocyclone system is usually tailor-made in oil and gas production and has strong coupling between its three-phase gravity separator and hydrocyclones, which re-sult in difficult of model-based control design and disturbance rejection. Towards this end, this paper studies the model-free tracking control of de-oiling hydrocyclone systems against slug-ging disturbances and a Q-learning-based robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> tracking control scheme is proposed. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> tracking control problem is formulated as a cascade two-player zero-sum differential game, and the optimal state feedback control solution is learned using the Q-learning algorithm. The salient feature of the proposed solution is that system dynamics knowledge is not required and disturbances sensitivity of the de-oiling hydrocyclone system can be significantly reduced. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Bipartite Consensus Control for Fixed and Switching Multi-Agent Systems via State Feedback, Observer and Output Feedback
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper studies the bipartite consensus problem of high-order linear leader-following multi-agent systems (MASs) under fixed and switching topologies. All followers are divided into two competitive subsets, where the followers in the same subset are cooperative. In different topological environment, we respectively design three different distributed controllers via state feedback, observer and output feedback to achieve the so-called bipartite consensus with the structural balanced condition. Finally, numerical examples are given to demonstrate the analytic results.

articleTitle: Adaptive Control of Virtual Synchronous Generator Based RBF Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: When the power of the distribution power generation system of the microgrid fluctuates greatly, the output power and frequency of the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) are prone to oscillate. Vibration can be suppressed by adjusting the moment of inertia and damping coefficient. However, due to the nonlinear relationship between these two parameters and frequency, this paper proposes a RBF neural network to improve the VSG moment of inertia and damping coefficient adaptive control strategy. Finally, MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform is used to build the microgrid model and improved VSG algorithm, and simulation experiments are carried out. The results verify the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Global Motion Planning for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Automation
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Global motion planning is a critical problem to be explored in the context of autonomous UAVs. It involves two main objectives: finding an optimal path between a source and destination, and effectively avoiding obstacles during autonomous missions. This involves both path planning and trajectory planning, although some research proposals solely concentrate on defining control policies for autonomous obstacle avoidance. This paper presents a technique for global motion planning to address path planning and trajectory planning sequentially. The mission path is planned after defining no-fly zones using an extended version of QGroundControl developed specifically for this purpose. The RRT* algorithm from the OMPL is then employed to generate a path that effectively avoids the defined obstacles. The flight path is continually updated whenever an obstacle is detected to ensure UAV safety during autonomous missions. This update process incorporates the initial mission path, the UAV's current GPS coordinates, and the output from the obstacle detector. It relies on machine learning models for obstacle detection and collision prediction, and involves generating waypoints to avoid obstacles while following the initial flight path. The proposed technique has been tested in the Gazebo simulator and appears to be suitable for autonomous missions in outdoor environments.

articleTitle: A Coal-Rock Cutting Hardness Recognition Model Based on CNN-PN
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Existing methods for accurate recognition of coal-rock cutting hardness by shearer machines in complex environments face challenges in timely adjusting the drum speed and traction velocity to adapt to changes in coal-rock cutting hardness. In this paper, we propose a Coal-Rock Cutting Hardness Recognition Model based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) - Prototype Network (PN). Firstly, multiple sensor signals are utilized to generate high-dimensional data, which is then fed into CNN for feature extraction. Subsequently, the features extracted by the convolutional neural network are input into the PN, which calculates the embedding center distances for each category, obtaining representative prototype vectors. The similarity between prototype vectors is measured using Euclidean distance, and these prototype vectors form different groups. Thirdly, the Adam algorithm is employed to optimize the network model, enabling better adaptation to data distribution differences and improving training effectiveness. Finally, the proposed model is validated through experiments using collected data. Unlike traditional machine learning approaches that require extensive manual feature extraction and data preprocessing for coal-rock cutting hardness recognition, which affects recognition accuracy and efficiency, the proposed method overcomes these limitations and can directly classify raw multi-sensor data signals during coal-rock cutting by shearer machines while effectively recognizing coal-rock cutting hardness. Experimental results demonstrate an average recognition rate of 99.64% for the proposed model, indicating high recognition accuracy and good generalization performance.

articleTitle: Research on Industrial Human Action Recognition Based on Improved SlowFast
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In industrial site, safety accidents caused by unsafe actions of personnel are unfortunately common. Swift and accurate recognition of human actions can timely alert on-site personnel and reduce the risk of injuries and property damage caused by production accidents. This paper proposes an improved action recognition algorithm based on the Slow Fast framework. It introduces the C3DS attention module and the MH-C3DS multi-head attention module to enhance the network's capability in extracting different action features. The original single-classifier structure is transformed into a multi-branch structure with independent classifiers to improve the recognition accuracy for multiple actions. A dataset of human actions in industrial site is constructed to analyze the algorithm's recognition performance in real-world industrial site. With the incorporation of attention modules and the multi-classifier structure, the recognition accuracy of the algorithm is improved by 9.8%, achieving an overall accuracy of 77.4% for the improved recognition algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate that the improved recognition algorithm performs well in real industrial site, validating the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm enhancements.

articleTitle: Analysis of Maximum Permissible Delay-Time Limit for Stability of PV-Battery Grid-Tied System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) power generation is an effective means of harnessing solar energy and plays a crucial role in the operation of microgrid systems. The DC microgrid system based on PV power generation boasts the advantages of simplified control and reduced power losses. Within the microgrid, sources, storage units, and loads are connected to the DC bus via DC-DC converters while communication between modules is facilitated through a network dedicated to such purpose However, the transmission of control signals through the shared network results in time delay, rendering the microgrid a time-delay system and leading to potential instability. Therefore, it is crucial to establish the maximum permissible delay-time limit (MPDL). In this paper, the PV-battery grid-tied system is modeled, and the delay stability boundary is analyzed. Finally, we verify the MPDL stability boundary through simulation.

articleTitle: Cooperative Tracking of Autonomous Underwater Vehicle with Quantized Relative Measurement
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Cooperative control of autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) is becoming increasingly important in ocean exploration and underwater operations, one important control objective is ensure a group of AUVs to maintain formation and track the predefined trajectory. This paper proposes a cooperative tracking controller for a group of AUVs with quantized relative measurement information. By using the backstepping methods, the position controller is first designed and then a suitable angle controller is derived such that the problem of cooperative formation tracking of AUVs is solved. Under the proposed control laws, Lyapunov function method is used to prove the stability of the closed-loop system. Compared to existing approaches, the quantized relative measurements are considered, in which the continuous communication among the AUVs is avoided. Simulation results show that the proposed controller can achieve the control objectives.

articleTitle: Co-Design of Underwater Detection and Communication-Part II: Communication-Based Shared Waveform
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Compared with the integrated waveform of the Part I, its waveform has stronger detection ability but the communication signal is suppressed. This will not be conducive to networking positioning. Based on this, a comprehensive waveform design scheme for underwater detection and communication based on direct sequence spread spectrum and Gaussian min-imum shift keying (GMSK) waveform is proposed. The scheme realizes the detection of the target by collecting the echo of the communication signal reflected by the target. In this scheme, the communication signal is expanded, and then modulated onto the carrier as an integrated signal through GMSK modulation. The detection performances of minimum shift keying (MSK), GMSK and underwater acoustic modulation signals under different parameters are compared by a fuzzy function. The underwater echo model is established, and the performance of MSK and GMSK target estimation is analyzed. For the echo signal, it is first demodulated and then despread, and the PN code at the receiving end needs to be synchronized with the PN code at the transmitting end. And the bit error rate of the integrated signal is analyzed. Simulation results show that the designed integrated waveform is effective.

articleTitle: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles based on Spatial-Temporal Model with Flight Data
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Anomaly detection of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) has gained great importance to guarantee safety. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised anomaly detection framework based on spatial-temporal feature learning of available multivariate flight data. First, a spatial-temporal prediction model is designed based on convolutional neural network (CNN) and long short-term memory (LSTM), which can extract the spatial-temporal features from multivariate time series sensor variables in a sequential manner. Then, a low-pass filter is utilized to smooth the residuals to decrease the impact of noise on anomaly detection performance. Finally, anomaly detection is achieved by comparing the smoothed residuals with a statistical threshold. A real flight dataset is used to verify its validation and experimental results demonstrated that our proposed method outperforms several state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: A Human-Computer Interaction Method for Intelligent Pan-Tilt Based on the Combination of Head-Eye Posture
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an intelligent pan-tilt human-computer interaction system that can be utilized for distance teaching through a combination of head-eye posture. The system obtains real-time head-eye posture information of the remote teacher using an ordinary camera on the teacher side. The data is then sent to the student side to drive the pan-tilt in real-time to track and rotate to the corresponding field of view. The real-time status value is returned to the teacher side computer to achieve remote pan-tilt human-computer interaction. The proposed method employs the ERT (Ensemble of Regression Trees) face alignment method of cascade regression, which is a gradient boosting-based regression tree method used to extract feature points from real-time frames. The coordinate information of feature points is stored to the set, and then the face contour area is traversed and filtered to select the target object and perform head pose estimation. During the experiments, users provided positive feedback on the system's real-time performance and accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate that the average recognition rate of the head-eye pose combination algorithm can reach 98.33%, and the average accuracy of the pan-tilt interactive experiment can reach 94.35%. The proposed method overcomes the limitations of remote space vision, allowing users to obtain multi-dimensional full-view video according to their posture changes. This provides great convenience for distance learning, and the system has many potential applications in the military, medicine, and transportation fields.

articleTitle: Learning Dynamic Graph Structures for Sea State Estimation with Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Accurate estimation of sea state is crucial for the advancement of autonomous ships, given the complexity and dynamics of the marine environment. However, traditional methods for classifying sea states suffer from drawbacks such as low accuracy, limited coverage, and high cost. The emergence of deep learning has provided a significant breakthrough in sea state estimation (SSE). Nonetheless, existing models lack the ability to dynamically interact with features from various sensors. In this study, we propose a deep neural network model, named DynamicSSE, which aims to autonomously learn the dynamic correlations among sensors located at different positions. This facilitates the interaction between sensors, enabling the generation of more valuable features for prediction. DynamicSSE comprises two primary modules: a feature extraction module and a dynamic graph structure construction module. By combining a series of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and a long short-term memory network (LSTM), our model effectively captures graph structures and dependencies over both long and short time periods. Moreover, our proposed approach demonstrates its superiority through experimental results on two ship motion datasets, supported by a comparative analysis with the baseline approach. Additionally, an ablation study highlights the significance of each component in our model.

articleTitle: Semantic Line Map: A Novel Visual Map Representation Scheme for Autonomous Driving Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: High-precision maps are a crucial require-ment for autonomous driving systems, yet traditional mapping approaches often encounter issues related to storage, efficiency, and positioning speed. To address these issues, a new map representation scheme called “Semantic Line Map (SEML)” has been proposed, which combines deep learning techniques with an efficient storage method based on line segments, using road linear landmarks as carriers to establish a semantic line segment map of the road environment. To achieve visual line segment semantic segmentation mapping, we utilize camera data and employ the COLMAP algorithm for 3D scene reconstruction based on motion inference structure. We also use the PSPNet semantic segmentation network to obtain end-to-end semantic segmentation of 2D images. The resulting segmented images undergo line segment extraction and computation of 3D line segment positions, enabling us to obtain the final 3D semantic line graph. Our experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm is efficient and capable of achieving high-fidelity mapping solutions.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method of Bearings Under Variable Operating Condition Based on HFL-TL
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low accuracy of bearing fault diagnosis caused by data distribution differences in traditional machine learning algorithms under variable operating conditions, this paper proposes a bearing fault diagnosis method that combines horizontal federated learning and transfer learning. Firstly, data is divided according to the type of operating conditions, and distributed to each participant according to the distributed network model architecture; Then, the federated average algorithm is used to continuously interact and fine-tune model parameters between the coordinator and participants during the transfer learning process; Finally, a federated model suitable for classification of bearing health status under variable operating conditions is obtained. Through experimental verification, the diagnostic accuracy of this method reaches above 99% and has good adaptability. This method utilizes a distributed model architecture to fuse bearing operation data under different operating conditions, and conducts parameter transfer learning under multi-party collaboration, providing a new idea for bearing fault diagnosis methods.

articleTitle: Research on Improving ST-GCN for Recognition of Unsafe Actions of Personnel in Industrial Site
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In industrial scenarios, incidents caused by unautho-rized activities such as smoking and phone usage by personnel have been occurring frequently, resulting in irreparable losses. Real-time detection and timely warning of unsafe actions among on-site personnel have significant implications for ensuring fac-tory safety and protecting the lives of individuals. In this paper, we propose an industrial scenarios personnel unsafe action recognition algorithm based on improved ST-GCN, adding the pose estimation algorithm (Alphapose) to improve the spatial-temporal graph convolutional network ST-GCN to enhance the action recognition accuracy; introducing the adaptive attention mechanism module SENet to enhance the feature extraction capability of the model for unsafe action; The YOLOX network is used to pre-process the input photos in order to reduce the influence of the factory's complex background on action recognition and increase the algorithm's recognition precision for employee activity. To address the limitation of limited data availability for industrial personnel unsafe action, a self-constructed dataset specific to industrial scenarios is established to alleviate the constraints on algorithm generalization. Based on this dataset, ablation comparative experiments are designed to analyze the improvement effects of different enhancement operations on the original algorithm. The experimental results demonstrate an overall increase in detection accuracy by 6.6 % after the proposed improvements. Specifically, the recognition accuracy for unsafe actions such as smoking and phone usage achieves 94.0 %. The experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed detection algorithm enhancements in real industrial scenarios, validating their practicality and performance.

articleTitle: A Robustness Enhanced Capsule Network with Regularization
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper aims to guarantee the robustness of capsule networks (CapsNets) by regularization in the construction of primary capsules and higher-level capsules. A novel CapsN et, namely robustness enhanced CapsNet with regularization (RE-CapsN et) has been put forward by exploiting the equivariant spatial relationship and the invariant descriptors of parts. The main idea of RE-CapsNet is three-fold: 1) the regularization for poses and descriptors of capsules combined with attention modules is introduced to establish the primary capsules; 2) the utilization of regularization contributes greatly to the robustness, and the adoption of attention modules and regularization gives rise to good interpretability of RE-CapsNet; 3) the comparison experiments on several datasets reveal the RE-CapsNet generalizes better on unfamiliar viewpoints with affine transformations.

articleTitle: A Method for Constructing Semantic Navigation Maps in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: The field of modern autonomous driving and unmanned systems places significant importance on planning and semantic navigation tasks for autonomous vehicles. The successful execution of these tasks relies heavily on mapping and localization technologies. We propose a method to address the difficulty of using trajectory maps of autonomous vehicle cameras in complex environments for planning. The proposed method constructs a topological map that is convenient for subsequent planning and semantic navigation. To enhance the integration of trajectory maps with topological maps, we employ the ORB-SLAM2 algorithm to create the camera's trajectory map, and we extract the keyframe information to obtain frames from the data. These extracted keyframes are then fed sequentially into a junction recognition network that utilizes ResNet18 transfer learning. Then we connect the resulting nodes that are recognized as junctions to generate the camera's topological map. The integration of trajectory and topological maps has been found to be advantageous in improving the planning and navigation abilities of ground robots.

articleTitle: Dynamic Event-triggered Robust Adaptive Practical Fixed-Time Trajectory Tracking Control for Underactuated AUVs
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper develops an event-triggered robust adaptive fixed-time trajectory tracking control scheme for underactuated autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) in the presence of uncertain dynamics and unknown time-varying disturbances. Here, a dynamic event-triggered mechanism (DETM) is created to reduce the transmission frequency of control commands drastically. The compound uncertain term caused by uncertain model parameters and disturbances is transformed into linearly parametric form with only one unknown parameter. By incorporating the above and a smooth function into the backstepping design tool, the fixed-time trajectory tracking control of AUVs is achieved. The theoretical analysis indicates that the tracking errors can converge to a small set around the origin in a fix time under proposed control scheme, while all signals in the AUV trajectory tracking close-loop control system are bounded. Simulation results on an AUV validate the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed control scheme.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling Method of Centralized Heating System Based on Hybrid Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper proposes an online simulation method for district heating systems, which combines the mechanistic model and the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm for modeling the district heating systems. The proposed model can visualize the thermal behavior and energy flow of the district heating systems during operation. The model considers the heat exchange stations, the heat network and the heat users as interconnected entities, and takes into account the relevant parameters such as heat load, pipe characteristics and heat transfer coefficient. Moreover, the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to optimize the parameters in the mechanistic model in real time through iteration, in order to improve the accuracy of the model. Finally, the model is validated using the data from an existing district heating system. The results show that combining the mechanistic model and the particle swarm optimization algorithm can accurately simulate the district heating system.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Impulsive Control of Multi-line Re-entrant Manufacturing Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This study focuses on the production control problem of the re-entrant manufacturing systems (RMSs) in the presence of product yield loss and couplings of multiple production lines. Initially, to describe and handle the complex dynamics of the RMSs, a nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equation (PDE) is employed and a Takagi-Sugeno (T-S) fuzzy-model-based impulsive control scheme is proposed. Then, the stability criteria for the RMSs are obtained by leveraging a time-dependent Lyapunov function. Subsequently, we propose a novel robust fuzzy impulsive controller which operates at specific impulsive instants and stages of the plant. Not only can the RMSs respond quickly to market demand when adapting the feeding rate to real-time demand, but also the bandwidth occupation and the communication cost are significantly reduced. Finally, a numerical example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed impulsive control method.

articleTitle: Dynamic Multi-Robot Path Planning in Narrow-Lane Environments with One-Way Constraint
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the rapid development of the logistics industry, the path planning problem for automated guided vehicles (AGVs) in warehousing systems has become a prominent research topic. Traditional multi-robot path planning algorithms often perform poorly in narrow-lane environments found in warehouses. This paper proposes an improved dynamic multi-robot path planning algorithm specifically tailored for narrow-lane environments. By constraining the traversal directions within narrow lanes and dynamically determining the optimal directions, this algorithm achieves efficient multi-robot path planning and enhances the quality of robot paths. The effectiveness of the algorithm is theoretically proven in this paper. Extensive simulation data demonstrates that our algorithm efficiently generates high-quality paths in high-density narrow-lane warehouse environments.

articleTitle: Robust $H_{\infty}$ Output Regulation of Nonlinear Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of output regulation for discrete-time nonlinear systems subject to unknown disturbances. Differing from the traditional output regulation problem, this work does not aim at accurately compensating for disturbances, but attenuating their effects within a desired bound. Towards this end, the output regulation problem is formulated as a robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> output regulation problem subject to an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{2}$</tex> -gain condition. To solve the robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H_{\infty}$</tex> output regulation problem, the power series approach is applied to obtain analytical solution of nonlinear regulator equations, which transfers the output regulation problem into a stability problem. An optimal state-feedback control solution based on linear quadratic regulator (LQR) is synthesized to guarantee the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{2}$</tex> -gain condition of the closed-loop control system. Simulation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Distributed Enclosing Control of Second-order Multi-Agent Systems with An Unknown Dynamic Target
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this article, we study the enclosing control problem for a group of agents of second-order dynamics with a moving target of unknown velocity. In particular, only one pathfinder has access to the relative position information of the target, and the target velocity is modeled as a dynamic signal generated by an exogenous linear system. Using the local relative position measurements, an observer of the target position is developed for each agent, based on which an estimator is designed for each agent to estimate the dynamic target velocity. Furthermore, based on the estimates of the target position and target velocity, a distributed control law is proposed for each agent consisting of distance regulation respect to the target and angle repulsion to its neighbors in conjunction with compensation of the target velocity. It is theoretically shown that the multi-agent system can globally asymptotically track the dynamic target with a circular formation of desired radius and arbitrary interval pattern. Finally, the proposed control law is shown to be effective by a simulation example.

articleTitle: Coal-Rock Interface Image Segmentation Based on U2Net Model with Coordinate Attention
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: Fast and accurate extraction of segmented images of coal-rock interfaces is one of the most important technologies to realize intelligent operation of comprehensive mining face. In this paper, we propose a multi-mechanism fusion U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Net model for recognizing coal-rock interfaces with complex backgrounds and diverse morphologies. We construct the basic network module by replacing the ordinary convolution in RSU with depth-divisible convolution and expansion convolution; add the coordinate attention mechanism in the last layer of the sampling stage of the improved RSU module to construct a new residual structure; and combine this residual structure with the U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Net model to construct a new U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Net model to realize the automatic learning of segmented images of coal-rock interfaces. Among them, the expansion convolution can obtain a larger sensory field without reducing the resolution; the depth separable convolution helps to simplify the model; the coordinate attention mechanism can suppress the interference of each residual block in the encoding and decoding process, and improve the model performance at a small cost. Compared with the semantic segmentation models commonly used in deep learning, this method improves the accuracy of extracting features from different stages of coal rock images, reduces the model training cost, accelerates the convergence speed of the model, and improves the model's anti-interference. Experiments were conducted to compare U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Net-CA-DC with four semantic segmentation networks (FCN, SegNet, UNet, and U<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>Net) to verify the effectiveness of the improved model. The accuracy of the method is 95.31% and the mIOU is 93.46% on real coal rock image datasets collected from actual underground wells. The experimental results show that the method provides a new solution for coal rock image segmentation detection and can provide data support for coal rock image segmentation.

articleTitle: Path Following Control of Underactuated AUV Based on Improved Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In this paper, an improved model predictive control (MPC) method using line-of-sight (LOS) for precise path following control is proposed. First, simplify the motion model of the underactuation five degree of freedom (DOF) autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV), Yunfan-04. The LOS guidance method provides precise heading instructions based on the line of sight position between the AUV and target. The MPC algorithm is used to generate an optimal control strategy based on the dynamic model of AUV to control the following motion of AUV. In order to optimize the path following performance, the problem formula is transformed into an optimization problem with constraints, and the optimal control input is solved. Simulation experiments validate our approach. The LOS and MPC-based method outper-forms traditional methods in accuracy and robustness, achieving stable and precise path following. This work provides valuable insights for developing AUV control systems.

articleTitle: Research on Collision Avoidance of Unmanned Surface Vehicle Based on Improved DDPG
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper addresses the collision avoidance of the underactuated unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) in the environment of random static obstacles based on an improved deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm. An improved algorithm based priority experience replay (PER) is developed to control the USV. Furthermore, the design of a marine environment includes obstacles with random initial positions. Moreover, the USV is modeled with the Norrbin model and the reward function set complies with the model and requirements of collision avoidance. The advantages of the developed collision avoidance scheme are that first, it could effectively prevent the emergence of paths that do not satisfy the actual navigation requirements of the USV and the PER mechanism can improve the USV collision avoidance accuracy rate; second, the designed environment is highly random, which is crucial for solving the problem that the method lacks practical usefulness. In addition, the proposed reward function optimizes the USV's trajectory so that it satisfies the requirements for both collision avoidance and appropriate USV motion. These features make the algorithm more useful. Finally, simulation and comparative experiments verify the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimal Path Planning Method for Emergency Repair Based on Heating GIS System
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: With the continuous development of GIS., its application is increasingly widespread and has a great impact in many aspects., and the shortest path algorithm is an essential method based on the realization of the shortest path selection. In this paper, an improved path planning research method of ant colony algorithm is proposed for the optimal path planning problem of multiple heat exchange stations that need to be repaired at one time. Firstly., a reward and punishment mechanism is used to update the pheromones on the paths, and limits are set on the maximum and minimum values of each path pheromone respectively., so that the convergence speed of the algorithm can be effectively improved; secondly., an adaptively adjusted amplification factor is introduced into the heuristic function to improve the difference of heuristic information of neighboring nodes., so that the ants search in the direction of the optimal path; then, by adjusting the heuristic function factor., the pheromone volatility factor and pheromone factor are dynamically adjusted to improve the search speed of the ant colony and make the algorithm converge quickly. Finally., an improved optimal path analysis method of the ant colony algorithm is proposed., and the optimal path algorithm is implemented on a GIS platform., and the performance of the algorithm is analyzed.

articleTitle: Visual SLAM Algorithm Based on Deep Learning Feature Extraction and Mismatch Elimination
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: To address the problem of poor system robustness of visual SLAM under sparse texture environment and fast camera rotation conditions, this paper improves the front-end based on the ORB-SLAM2 framework. The front end uses the Geometric Correspondence Network v2 (GCNv2) neural network based on deep learning to extract feature points. Due to the local characteristics of image features, there are mismatches of feature points. Fast approximate nearest neighbor algorithm (FLANN) and progressive sampling consistency algorithm (PROSAC) are used for feature matching and mismatch removal. Tested on the TUM public dataset, the experimental results show that the improved algorithm has no tracking loss under sparse texture environment and fast camera rotation conditions, more uniform distribution of extracted feature points, higher efficiency of false match rejection, smaller absolute trajectory error of the system, higher localization accuracy, and better robustness.

articleTitle: Research on Long and Short Term Heat Load Prediction of Central Heating
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: In response to the heat load prediction problems of centralized heating, Various prediction models for short-term and long-term heat load prediction are summarized and verified for their applicability. Firstly, the historical data is preprocessed by removing abnormal data and normalizing the sample dataset. Secondly, models including the autoregressive integrated moving average model (ARIMA) and multivariate grey prediction model (GM(1,n)) are selected and built for predictive analysis. Then, the mean square error (MSE) criterion is used to evaluate the models by calculating the corresponding MSE values for the predictive results of different models. Finally, historical data from a heating company in Dalian is used as the research object to verify the applicability of different prediction models by using actual historical production data.

articleTitle: Detection of Alzheimer's Disease using Deep Learning: An Optimized Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 6th International Conference on Intelligent Autonomous Systems (ICoIAS)
abstract: This paper suggests a new CNN that requires just a few parameters to diagnose AD and is perfect for training on smaller datasets. Compared to existing state-of-the-art models, the proposed model uses a more optimized technique to identify the early stages of Alzheimer's disease. The image is sharpened and normalized as part of the preparation phase to help the model learn more quickly and succinctly. We used a bespoke CNN model that makes precise predictions with minimum parameters. Five Convolutional layers and three fully connected layers, which have equally learned samples from each class, make up the proposed model. The approach was compared using a variety of accuracy metrics, such as accuracy, AUC, precision, recall, and Fl-Score, as well as categorical cross-entropy loss, self, and other comparisons. To accurately forecast the method, several trials were carried out. The values for the evaluation measures are as follows: accuracy, AUC, precision, recall, fl-score, and loss are 99.95%, 99.99%, 99.97%, 99.95%, and 0.0016 respectively. According to simulation results, the proposed model performs better than existing cutting-edge models in all evaluation metrics.
